findings.title: Light-theme color silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness for embedded post author link
findings.body: For `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` the old rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, i.e. the light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness in the first (light-theme) argument and uses `100 - X` for the `$secondary` argument. The result is that on light themes the author name in an expanded in-reply-to/reply block is rendered ~70% lightened primary (very close to the background), a noticeable contrast/accessibility regression unrelated to the stated purpose of the PR. The first argument should stay `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` with `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)` as the dark branch.

findings.title: Group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`; it is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The light-theme value was changed from 30% to 50%, so the member name becomes lighter than before on light themes and is now indistinguishable from the sibling `.title` (which was intentionally dimmer at 50%). Per the PR's own convention the pair should be `30%` / `70%`.

findings.title: Mobile group member name light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: `.user-stream .group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This alters light-theme rendering (name becomes lighter and identical to the deliberately dimmer `.title` below it) instead of only adding dark-theme support. Should be `30%` / `70%` to preserve the existing light-theme appearance.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 light-theme lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and now resolves to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` on light themes. The heading text in the mobile topic map therefore becomes considerably lighter than before and matches the subordinate `h4` (also 50%), removing the visual hierarchy. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/topic-post.scss` was converted correctly as `20%` / `80%`; the mobile rule should match.

findings.title: custom-message-length light-theme lightness inverted (70% -> 30%), diverging from desktop
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`; the new value is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, i.e. the light-theme color is now much darker (30% instead of 70%). `desktop/modal.scss` for the same class was converted as `70%` / `30%`, so mobile and desktop now render this hint text differently on light themes. One of the two is wrong; the light branch should keep the original 70%.

findings.title: Missed conversion: category badge-notification still uses scale-color($primary) only
findings.body: `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` still uses `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)` while every comparable rule in this file was converted to `dark-light-choose(...)`. On dark color schemes `$primary` is the light text color, so scaling its lightness up by 50% yields a near-white value, making this badge brighter than normal text instead of dimmer — exactly the defect this PR is fixing elsewhere.

findings.title: Comment describing the topic-list default color is now stale
findings.body: The comment above the coldmap rules states "the default for table cells in topic list is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)". After this PR the topic-list cell default is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))` (see `common/base/_topic-list.scss`), so the comment no longer matches the code and will mislead anyone tuning these heat/cold map colors.
